ai.title: Manicode file edit format shifts to whole-file content with diff
ai.summary: Manicode prompt instructions replaced explicit `<old>`/`<new>` blocks with whole-file content using `// ... existing code` markers. `processFileBlock` now detects existing files and calls new `generateDiffBlocks` helper, which prompts the model to convert shorthand markers into precise string-replacement diff pairs. File processing switched from sequential `await` to concurrent `Promise.all` with regex-based block extraction. Covers `src/manicode.ts` only; no user-facing CLI or Web surface changes.

eli5.text: The developer-facing instructions that guide how file edits are written changed: instead of marking old and new sections separately, you now paste the whole file and use comments like '... existing code...' to show what stays. Behind the scenes, the system reads those shorthand comments and converts them into precise before-and-after snippets to apply. Files are also processed at the same time instead of one after another, which should make multi-file edits feel quicker. This is live today for people writing edits inside this tooling, but it doesn't change the final result you see.

ai.title: Manicode standalone package
ai.summary: Extracted manicode into standalone package. Renamed src/manicode.ts to index.ts. Added local claude.ts, util/array.ts, util/object.ts. Updated package.json name, scripts, dependencies. Added tsconfig.json, updated .gitignore.

eli5.text: The manicode tool, which helps automate parts of software development, has been split into its own separate package instead of living inside a larger shared codebase. If you looked at the project, you would see a new setup file for compiling the code, an updated project list of required libraries, and the main code renamed and reorganized into smaller, self-contained helper files. Several old project-specific files and debug logs were also cleaned up from the shared ignore list, and a few new utility helpers for working with lists and objects were added locally.

ai.title: Add backend WebSocket server
ai.summary: New backend server routes prompts to Claude via WebSocket. index.ts connects to ws://localhost:3000 instead of direct execution. backend/claude.ts handles Anthropic streaming. File selection logic commented out.

eli5.text: When you run the tool, it no longer talks to the AI helper directly, instead it opens a live text channel to a separate program on your computer that manages the back-and-forth. That helper program connects to the Claude AI and streams replies back piece by piece, so you see words appear gradually rather than waiting for the whole answer at once. The new system also stops looking for specific files to work with, so it can no longer pick or edit a file on its own from this interface. This is live today and only works if that background program is running.

ai.title: Add @manicode/common workspace for shared utilities
ai.summary: Introduced @manicode/common workspace containing shared utility functions like removeUndefinedProps and filterDefined. Updated backend and root packages to import from @manicode/common instead of local util paths. Configured TypeScript project references and path mappings for monorepo structure. Backend package renamed to @manicode/backend with proper dist output paths.

eli5.text: The team pulled the assistant's shared helper functions (like cleaning up data and filtering lists) into a single shared code library that both the main program and the backend server can use. Instead of each part keeping its own copy of these helpers, they now both pull from this one common library, which keeps things consistent and easier to maintain. You would notice the backend server now builds its code into a dedicated output folder and starts up from a cleaner project layout, but the assistant's behavior itself stays the same.

ai.title: Split monolithic index.ts into src modules
ai.summary: Refactored `index.ts` by extracting WebSocket client logic, system prompt generation, and file block parsing into dedicated modules (`src/websocket-client.ts`, `src/system-prompt.ts`, `src/file.ts`). This separates concerns, allowing `index.ts` to focus on orchestration while importing typed helpers for communication and prompt construction. The `tsconfig.json` updated to include new source files and set `outDir`. Internal architecture change with no user-facing behavior modification.

eli5.text: The team split a large, all-in-one control file into smaller, dedicated files that each handle a specific job: one manages the connection to the assistant, one builds the instructions it works from, and one reads and writes code files. From a reader's point of view, nothing looks different right away because the program still does the same things, but the project now keeps each kind of work in its own organized space, so adding or adjusting one part (like how file exchanges look) won't accidentally break the others.

ai.title: Refactor manicode prompt and project root resolution
ai.summary: Removed two-step file selection logic in `manicode`, switching to direct single-prompt execution. Defined `projectRoot` in `src/index.ts` and `src/system-prompt.ts` to replace `__dirname` for consistent path resolution. Deleted commented-out `getExportedTokensForFiles` logic and unused imports. Scope limited to internal core files; no user-facing behavior changes.

eli5.text: The tool that handles coding tasks now skips a separate planning step and jumps straight to working on your request in one go. It also fixes how the tool locates your project files so paths resolve consistently, removing some old, unused helper code along the way. There are no visible changes for you: the tool still behaves the same from your perspective.

ai.title: Add prettier format script
ai.summary: Added `format` script and `prettier` devDependency to `package.json`. Removed `prettier-plugin-sql` from `.prettierrc` plugins array. Scope limited to root configuration.

eli5.text: A developer added a new one-click command that will automatically tidy up the project's text files so they all look uniformly formatted. This command is now part of the project's standard toolkit, making it easier for anyone on the team to keep the code clean. At the same time, the developer removed a specialized add-on that was previously being used to format database files. If you looked at the project's configuration file, you'd see these changes reflected there.
